original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-snake}
\begin{reference}
\cite[III, Lemma 3.3]{Cartan-Eilenberg}
\end{reference}
Given a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
& X \ar[r] \ar[d]^\alpha &
Y \ar[r] \ar[d]^\beta &
Z \ar[r] \ar[d]^\gamma &
0 \\
0 \ar[r] & U \ar[r] & V \ar[r] & W
}
$$
of abelian groups with exact rows, there is a canonical exact sequence
$$
\Ker(\alpha) \to \Ker(\beta) \to \Ker(\gamma)
\to
\Coker(\alpha) \to \Coker(\beta) \to \Coker(\gamma)
$$
Moreover: if $X \to Y$ is injective, then the first map is
injective; if $V \to W$ is surjective, then the last
map is surjective.

stage_b_review_note: The pinned snake-lemma source assumes a commutative diagram of abelian groups with both rows exact. The draft preserves all three vertical maps, the full six-term kernel-to-cokernel exact sequence, and each separately conditional endpoint claim: injectivity from X→Y injective and surjectivity from V→W surjective. No endpoint assumption has been elevated to a global prerequisite.
